newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha prices ease in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha prices ease in subdued trade.

text.p: Naphtha prices fell in afternoon Tokyo trade on Monday in tandem with Friday's bearish crude markets, but activity was slow with the London market closed for a public holiday, traders said.

Open-spec naphtha for second-half October was assessed at $192.75/$194.00, down from late Friday's $195.50/$196.00. First-half November was quoted at $192.50/$193.50 on Monday. It was traded at $195.00 on Friday.
Inter-month naphtha spreads shrank slightly, with second-half October/second-half Nobember talked at plus $0.50/$1.25.
First-half October/first-half November was discussed at plus $1.00/$1.50.

In the physical naphtha market, a Japanese refiner bought one cargo to be delivered to Kawasaki between October 1 and October 10. The price could not be confirmed, but the level was said to be less than $3.50 over the mean of Japanese quotes.

The Trade Ministry said Japan's gas oil output in July hit a record high of 4.2 million kilolitres (kl), up 8.1 percent from a year ago. Gas oil imports in July totaled 148,000 kl, down 48.6 percent from the same period a year earlier.
